analysis.title: Taiwan Weekly Kickstart: TAIEX rallied 12% on a sharp Tech rebound alongside global tech recovery and policy support; QFII outflows moderated but shorts rose, while retail margin unwound and ETF inflows remained strong
key_insights: TAIEX and TPEx gained 12% and 10% on the week, outperforming MXAPJ by 7pp. Chemicals rose 16%, Tech rose sharply (TSMC +10%, other semis +16%, hardware +11%) and Capital Goods rose 9%. Utilities, Telcos, Mining and Autos (flat) lagged.

QFIIs net sold US$2.9bn of cash equities on the week, concentrated in Tech (TSMC -US$1.2bn, other Tech -US$3.1bn). They bought Industrials (+US$570mn) and Financials (+US$350mn) and added US$3.1bn to net-short futures positions.
Domestic funds net bought US$3.1bn broadly across sectors. Retail investors were modest net buyers of cash equities amid margin unwinds but kept adding ETF exposure.
ETFs saw US$5.8bn of inflows, led by broad-market passive (+US$2.2bn), active (+US$1.7bn), leveraged (+US$1.1bn) and dividend (+US$0.8bn) ETFs.

Consensus 2027E EPS rose 0.3%. 3Q26 results concluded with +74% yoy and +7% qoq EPS growth, a 4% aggregate beat but a 2% median miss. October sales rose 54% yoy (vs +50% in September), tracking ahead of consensus.
Exports rose 59% yoy, ahead of the 51% consensus (September +61%), on strong tech demand.

The short-selling limit was cut from 30% to 3% of 30-day ADV. Foreign trading activity has moderated since, and retail participation has increased alongside the activation of the National Stabilization Fund. Short interest still rose over the past week, possibly from investors establishing shorts ahead of tighter quota availability.

QFIIs have net sold US$54bn since early October, led almost entirely by Tech, and hedge funds have de-risked to near March exposure levels. Retail remains risk-on, with leveraged ETF exposure at US$15bn (0.9% of free float) on renewed inflows.
Margin-unwind risk has eased: margin loans fell US$2.5bn to US$13bn, the maintenance ratio recovered to about 165%, and the share of stocks below 130% fell to 27% from 39%.

In the November 2026 MSCI review Taiwan sees 2 of 15 additions and 4 of 10 deletions in the Standard/IMI benchmarks, effective after November 30. GS estimates US$3.8bn of gross two-way passive flows and US$450mn of net passive inflows.
